steps.observation: Work on this for 10 seconds; do not stop early. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
At a high level, a Transformer processes a sequence of tokens (words, subwords, etc.) by letting every position “look at” every other position in the sequence, and then passing the result through a small feed-forward network.  Key ideas:

1. Token Embeddings + Positional Encoding  
   • Each input token is mapped to a fixed-size vector (“embedding”).  
   • Since there’s no recurrence, we inject information about token order via added or concatenated “positional encodings.”

2. Self-Attention (“Scaled Dot-Product Attention”)  
   For each position i in the sequence:  
     a. Compute three vectors: Query Qi, Key Ki, and Value Vi (all linear projections of the embedding).  
     b. Score how well token i attends to token j by taking the dot product Qi·Kj, scaling by √d, then applying softmax over j.  
     c. The output at i is the weighted sum ∑j softmax(Qi·Kj/√d)·Vj.  
   This lets the model dynamically pool information from anywhere in the sequence.

3. Multi-Head Attention  
   • Instead of one big attention, use H parallel “heads,” each with its own Q/K/V projections.  
   • Concatenate their outputs and linearly project back to the model dimension.  
   • Allows the model to capture different types of relationships in different subspaces.

4. Position-wise Feed-Forward Network  
   • After multi-head attention, each position passes through the same small two-layer MLP (with ReLU or GELU).  
   • This injects per-position nonlinearity and expands representational power.

5. Residual Connections + Layer Norm  
   • Around both the multi-head attention block and the feed-forward block, add a “skip connection”:  
        output = LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x))  
   • Helps training stability and gradient flow.

6. Stacking Layers  
   • A “Transformer encoder” stacks N identical layers of (Multi-Head Attention → FFN).  
   • A “Transformer decoder” similarly stacks blocks, but each layer also has a cross-attention sublayer that lets decoder positions attend to encoder outputs.

7. Final Linear & Softmax (for language modeling or classification)  
   • In generation, the decoder’s last layer output for each position is linearly projected to the vocabulary size and softmaxed to yield next-token probabilities.

Conceptually, the power comes from:  
– letting each token directly consult every other token’s representation (via attention)  
– doing so in multiple “heads” to capture diverse patterns  
– stacking these blocks so that each layer refines the representations.
